title: Khokhloma pattern painting
summary: Khokhloma is a Russian craft from the Volga region in which wooden bowls, spoons and furniture are given a warm golden shine with a metal powder and then painted with red and black berries, curling leaves and grass sprigs. Heat in the oven turns the finish a deep, glowing gold.
howToPlay: Pick a colour and a mark from the strip under the panel: berries, rings, leaves, curls, grass and flowers.
Tap a square to paint it: the same mark appears in the matching squares turned round the middle, as on a plate.
Copy the small design above the panel, then press Check.
rules: The panel is a plate seen from above: whatever you paint is repeated in four turns around the centre.
A square scores only when its mark and its colour both match the design.
Painting the same mark and colour again, or using the eraser, clears it.
Three stars need a near-perfect copy; undo and clear are free.
heritageNote: Khokhloma takes its name from a village in the Nizhny Novgorod region of Russia, where painted wooden ware has been made since the seventeenth century and is still made by workshops and families today.
